extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates or graduate students studying algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Foundational definitions, constructions, and checkable properties for graded rings, the Proj construction, projective/quasiprojective schemes, and basic topological/algebraic properties of schemes (reducedness, integrality, Noetherian, quasicompact/quasiseparated, affine-local properties, varieties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Homogeneous element / homogeneous ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: An element of a Z-graded ring S is homogeneous if it lies in a single graded piece; a (graded) ideal I of S is homogeneous if it is generated by homogeneous elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, I is homogeneous iff for each element of I, every graded-piece (degree n piece) of that element lies in I; thus I decomposes into homogeneous pieces and inherits a natural Z-grading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closure properties of homogeneous ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: The collection of homogeneous ideals of a given Z-graded ring S is closed under sum, product, intersection, and radical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these closure properties when forming new homogeneous ideals (e.g., radicals or products remain homogeneous).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primality criterion for homogeneous ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: A homogeneous ideal I is prime if whenever a·b ∈ I for homogeneous a, b, then a ∈ I or b ∈ I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primality can be checked on homogeneous elements; exercises ask to show that if I is prime and homogeneous then this homogeneous-element condition characterizes it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization preserves grading for homogeneous localizations
rubrics_metrics.description: If T is a multiplicative subset of S consisting of homogeneous elements, then the localization T^{-1}S inherits a natural Z-grading (deg(1/f) = -deg(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used in constructing the affine pieces ((S_f)) and in defining ((S_f))_0 later in the Proj construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Z_{60}-graded (nonnegative) ring convention
rubrics_metrics.description: A Z_{60}-graded ring is a Z-graded ring with no elements of negative degree. For the remainder of the book, 'graded ring' refers to a Z_{60}-graded ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This convention is nonstandard; be aware when comparing with other literature.

For a graded ring S = 90_{i

rubrics_metrics.guidance: S_+ is used to single out the 'relevant' homogeneous prime ideals (those not containing S_+) when forming Proj; properties like 'geometrically irrelevant' are expressed via containment of S_+ in radicals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finitely generated graded ring over A
rubrics_metrics.description: S is a finitely generated graded ring over A (with S_0 = A) if S_+ is a finitely generated ideal (equivalently S is generated as an A-algebra by finitely many homogeneous elements of positive degree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 4.5.D shows the equivalence between S being a finitely generated graded A-algebra and S_+ being finitely generated as an ideal; use generators of S_+ to generate S as an algebra.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generated in degree 1
rubrics_metrics.description: S is generated in degree 1 if S is generated as an A-algebra by S_1 (equivalently the natural map Sym^0 S_1 -> S is a surjection).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition is often convenient (e.g., when interpreting sections as sections of line bundles); beware of alternative formulations in literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian criterion for graded rings
rubrics_metrics.description: A graded ring S over A is Noetherian iff A = S_0 is Noetherian and S is a finitely generated graded A-algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the equivalence (Exercise 4.5.D(b)) when checking Noetherian hypotheses for graded rings arising in geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points of Proj S
rubrics_metrics.description: The points of Proj S are the homogeneous prime ideals of S that do not contain the irrelevant ideal S_+ (i.e., the relevant homogeneous prime ideals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the analogue of points of Spec; thinking of homogeneous primes as cones helps visualize projective geometry (cones over affine pieces, 'plane at infinity' etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine building blocks of Proj: Spec((S_f)_0)
rubrics_metrics.description: For homogeneous f ∈ S_+ (positive degree), the affine building blocks for Proj S are Spec((S_f)_0), where (S_f) is the localization and ((S_f)_0) denotes the degree-0 piece of the graded ring (S_f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D(f) := Proj S \ V(f) will correspond to Spec((S_f)_0); these distinguished opens (for f homogeneous of positive degree) form an affine cover of Proj S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective distinguished opens form a base
rubrics_metrics.description: The distinguished open sets D(f) (as f runs through homogeneous elements of S_+) form a base for the Zariski topology on Proj S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One often works by checking statements on these D(f) and then gluing; D(f)995 are affine and satisfy D(f)995 ∩ D(g)=D(fg).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vanishing sets and Zariski topology on Proj
rubrics_metrics.description: For a set T of homogeneous elements of positive degree, define the projective vanishing set V(T) to be homogeneous prime ideals containing T but not S_+. V(f) and V(I) are defined similarly for homogeneous f and homogeneous ideals I ⊂ S_+; the V(I)'s satisfy the axioms for closed sets of a topology (the Zariski topology).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many affine facts carry over: e.g., D(f)995 = Proj S \ V(f); if fn ∈ I then f vanishes on V(I) etc.; use these for geometric arguments and to detect emptiness (radical containing S_+ iff V(I)=∅).

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence of primes under localization and degree-0 piece
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a bijection between prime ideals of ((S_f)_0) and homogeneous prime ideals of (S_f) (when f is homogeneous and invertible in the localized graded ring); this underlies the identification of D(f) with Spec((S_f)_0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bijection is subtle; the exercise gives hints (reduce to ring with a homogeneous invertible element and compare A_0 and homogeneous primes of A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure sheaf on Proj (gluing)
rubrics_metrics.description: On each D(f) the structure sheaf of Proj S is taken to be the structure sheaf of Spec((S_f)_0); these sheaves are glued together (checking pairwise and triple overlaps) to define the scheme Proj S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the isomorphisms between the Spec((S_f)_0) on overlaps (Exercises 4.5.K, 4.5.L) and the gluing lemma for sheaves (Exercise 2.5.D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of projective space
rubrics_metrics.description: Projective n-space over a ring A is defined as P^n_A := Proj A[x_0, ..., x_n], endowing it with the grading where each x_i has weight 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This basis-free Proj definition avoids choosing affine patches; the projective coordinates x_i are part of the data of P^n_A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective and quasiprojective schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme is projective over A if it is isomorphic to Proj S for some finitely generated graded A-algebra S with S_0 = A. A quasiprojective A-scheme is a quasicompact open subscheme of a projective A-scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often A is a field; quasiprojective can be characterized as an open subscheme of a projective scheme and is frequently equivalent to being of finite type over A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasicompactness
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme X is quasicompact iff it can be written as a finite union of affine open subschemes (equivalently the underlying topological space is quasicompact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used repeatedly: quasicompact schemes have closed points in closures of points, and many arguments reduce to checking finitely many affines when X is quasicompact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasiseparatedness
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme (or topological space) is quasiseparated if the intersection of any two quasicompact open subsets is quasicompact. Equivalently a scheme is quasiseparated iff the intersection of any two affine opens is a finite union of affine opens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quasiseparatedness is a mild technical hypothesis appearing with quasicompactness in many theorems; most schemes encountered in practice satisfy it (affine, locally Noetherian, separated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine-local properties and Affine Communication Lemma
rubrics_metrics.description: A property P of affine opens is affine-local (can be checked on any affine cover) if (i) it is stable under passing to distinguished opens Spec A_f, and (ii) if Spec A is covered by distinguished opens Spec A_{f_i} with each having P, then Spec A has P. The Affine Communication Lemma proves such properties can be checked on any affine cover of a scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this lemma to reduce checking many scheme-theoretic properties (e.g., reducedness, Noetherian, finite type) to checking them on an affine cover; this is the foundational 'glue' for affine-to-global reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian / locally Noetherian schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme X is locally Noetherian if it can be covered by affine opens Spec A with A Noetherian. If in addition X is quasicompact (finite such cover), then X is Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: Noetherian schemes have Noetherian underlying topological spaces, finitely many irreducible components, and many finiteness properties. Use Proposition 5.3.3 to pass Noetherian property between A and its localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite type / locally finite type over A
rubrics_metrics.description: An A-scheme X is locally of finite type over A if it can be covered by affines Spec B with each B a finitely generated A-algebra; if X is also quasicompact then X is of finite type over A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quasiprojective A-schemes are of finite type over A; finite-type hypotheses ensure many classical finiteness results and allow use of Nullstellensatz-style arguments over fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of variety (affine/projective) over a field k
rubrics_metrics.description: An affine k-scheme Spec A that is reduced and of finite type over k is an affine k-variety. A reduced (quasi)projective k-scheme is a (quasi)projective k-variety. Literature may sometimes require irreducibility or algebraically closed k in the definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check reducedness and finite-type hypotheses when translating between scheme language and classical varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reducedness of rings and schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring is reduced if it has no nonzero nilpotent elements. A scheme X is reduced if O_X(U) is reduced for every open U (equivalently all stalks have no nonzero nilpotents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reducedness is stalk-local and affine-local; for quasicompact schemes it suffices to check reducedness at closed points. Reduced locus need not be open in general, but it is open for locally Noetherian schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrality of schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme X is integral if it is nonempty and O_X(U) is an integral domain for every nonempty open U. Equivalently X is integral iff it is irreducible and reduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For integral X there is a generic point  and a function field K(X)=O_{X,}; restriction maps between nonempty open sets inject into K(X). Integrality is not purely stalk-local in general (disjoint unions show pathologies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasicompact schemes have closed points in closures
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is quasicompact, then every point has a closed point in its closure; every nonempty closed subset contains a closed point. In particular every nonempty quasicompact scheme has a closed point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fact is often used to check open properties by verifying them on closed points (density of closed points in many geometric situations).
